cells.tense: Now you are reading the harvest, and you find you can still eat from it.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Think of something small you owe — a reply, a borrowed dish, a few dollars — and settle it before anyone has to ask. Say nothing about it when you do.
cells.core:
You tend what is growing, and you can look at what came of it without pleading your case. The compass is quiet: what is owed, what is fair, who grew what. It knows without running numbers. The yield is on the table and you can call it what it is. When the season is decent you eat what you grew, and the people you fed know it was not a favour.

The hard part still comes next to a guest. Let the inner compass take one small case, and act before anyone asks. Because what this balance keeps asking of you is to be last to say what is owed. One returned thing, one quiet visit. The count stays honest that way, and the table stays open.
cells.sheetLine: You eat what you grew this year.
cells.verb: Surveying what transformation has grown, and counting it

cells.tense: You are bracing for next season before this one has been eaten, and the wait is winning.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: For one evening, sit with how this is actually going and do nothing about it. No watering, no plan, no next step. The pots can wait until morning.
cells.core:
You tend what is growing, and lately the harvest is being rushed before it ripens. What was patience has turned into checking the field every hour, adding water when nothing called for it, fretting at what is not up yet. The early frost you have not seen is the one you are working against. The plants have no way to answer that. When this pressure is working, it says less and waits more.

Sit with what is there before you do a single thing about the next thing. The feeling you have about how this is really going is the one witness still awake. Stay in it an evening; nothing is lost while you do. The field will still be there when you pick the feeling back up.
cells.sheetLine: You are pacing the field for a frost that has not come.
cells.verb: Surveying what transformation has grown, and counting it

cells.tense: The harvest came in while you were somewhere else, and you are still at the other door.
cells.act: do the next piece at the speed you can keep for a month, not the speed you can keep for a day
cells.ask: Pick the smallest piece of care undone around you — one pot, one letter, one shelf — and do it at a pace you could still keep in a month. Not faster.
cells.core:
You are supposed to have hands on what is growing here, and something in you has stepped off the row. The plants went on growing while you did not. The yield is out in the open, and the hands that should be weighing it have not come back through the gate. Nothing has broken; the finish simply arrived unwatched. Coming back does not need a speech about where you were.

Start with one small piece at a rhythm you could hold for a whole season, not a day's fit. The next and the next at the same speed. Momentum from one honest act pulls the missing grip back toward the row. Do less than you can; you will be here on Thursday anyway.
cells.sheetLine: You left the gate open and did not come back through.
cells.verb: Surveying what transformation has grown, and counting it

cells.tense: You keep the growing things level here for everyone, and you say you are only watching.
cells.act: declare the shape of it outward, plainly
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, what you keep steady here — what gets planted, when, who gets fed first when the tray is short. No arguing anyone into it. Then let it stand.
cells.core:
There is a keeper of what grows in your circle, and the keeper's own account is that they are just present. The planting order, the small daily turns, the one who gets fed first when the tray is short — none of that happened by itself, and none of it has ever been said in the open. The ones being tended have known for a while. They just wait for you to say it.

Name the shape out loud: what you keep alive here, and how. Once. If someone pokes a hole in the story, that is information, not a verdict. Saying it is the lighter thing, not the heavier one; what is kept by an unnamed hand is harder to keep than what is kept by a named one.
cells.sheetLine: The growing here keeps its shape because you keep it.
cells.verb: Surveying what transformation has grown, and counting it

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: in the Balanced cell I say the yield is checked against the person's own compass; the balanced face supports 'clear sense of what is right without obsessive calculation', so the joining of harvest to conscience is an inference, not a fact. A reader could reasonably say the harvest she counts is not moral at all but practical — what she planted got eaten or rained out. The asks survive being wrong: returning the small owed thing, sitting with what the heart knows, moving at a keeps-for-a-month pace, stating the order once are useful even if the compass is quiet or loud rather than accurate. The sentence that serves me more than the person is the Too Little line 'the plants went on growing while you did not' — it is vivid for me and tells her when her absence began, which the record does not say. Removed.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: the Balanced cell joins the drawn yield to the person's inner moral sense, but the balanced face only supports a felt-sense of fairness without obsessive calculation — the tie to harvest is inferred, not stated. A reader could reasonably say the harvest being counted is practical, not moral: what she planted, what got eaten, what the season left. The asks survive being wrong: returning something owed, sitting an evening with a settled feeling, one small job at a keepable pace, and stating the shape of the care are useful even if the compass is quiet or loud rather than accurate. The sentence that serves me more than the person is the Too Little opener about the room going on without a hand on it — it locates her absence and its duration, which the record does not say; it is being reworded to describe the capacity, not the history.
